In 1915, three years before the war even ended, a French pamphlet mapped out a Europe with no Germany on it at all.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The plan, published in Paris as 'L'Europe future de demain' by F. Pigeon, called for the total dissolution of Germany, Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire — plus abolishing the Kingdom of Prussia, the state that had built the German Empire in the first place.

2/ Germany west of the Rhine would go to France and Belgium, who'd also get back Alsace-Lorraine. East of the river, a demilitarised buffer zone would swallow Frankfurt under Allied control — the same idea Marshal Foch kept pushing for at Versailles in 1919.

3/ What was left of Germany would be broken into small, disarmed, deindustrialised states — Prussia (just Berlin and its west), Hanover, Saxony, Württemberg, Bavaria — a buffer strip between France and a Russian Empire annexing all German land east of the Oder.

4/ Austria-Hungary fared no better: dissolved into Italian, Serbian, Romanian and Swiss territory, with a rump Austrian state left holding Vienna, Moravia and Hungarian Burgenland. The Ottomans would be pushed back into deep Anatolia.

5/ Almost none of it happened. Washington opposed dismembering Germany outright, and the Russian Empire itself collapsed in 1917, two years before Versailles, before it could annex anything at all. Germany stayed one country, just smaller and disarmed.
